claims.summary: Under certificate-cube-erasure hypotheses, for every integer t>=1 put P=ordered product(1-F_i), H=sum_i prefix(1-F_j)Y_i and G_t=sum_(j<t)P^j. The supplied certificate C transforms to D_t=G_t H+P^t C, a certificate preserving placeholder-linearity, of size O(S+(m+t^2+1)(s+m+1)) and ordered unbounded-fan-in depth <=max(d,delta+4)+2. At every Boolean old point a, D_t-G_t H lies in the t-th power of the two-sided old-point ideal, so old-variable jets of order<t have the common small implicit representative G_t H. This is iterated cube normalization; it does not construct a certificate from nothing, enumerate all jets, preserve original degree/exact depth, or prove exact simulation-image preservation.
claims.assessment: Working costed iteration of the existing normalization, passed by the same fresh GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer after staged architecture comparison. No explicit jet-list or exact simulation-image complexity claim.
claims.rationale: Tests whether higher old-variable jets escape the already proved cube-value normalization, keeping representation size and depth explicit.
claims.next_action: Any jet-based certificate invariant must survive this polynomial-cost normalization or justify its exact resource/image restriction.
